mission: Test whether a retained infrastructure-promotion meta-selection prior produces cumulative value across later heterogeneous architecture/consumption decisions, despite adding prompt cost and not directly changing a product outcome when first created.
questionOrHypothesis: Does the Agent-first Infrastructure Promotion Rule behave like reusable decision capital across future choices, or would a fresh strong model make the same decisions from owner evidence without the prior?
evidenceSelection: Eight later A0/ACS decisions whose outcome/disposition is fixed by canonical closeouts. Each Provider-visible packet contains pre-decision owner evidence only; the canonical later disposition is evaluator-only.
strongBaseline: RAW: same decision packet and choice set, no infrastructure-promotion prior. The model is still told to prefer evidence and minimize unnecessary complexity.
minimalCandidateOrNoChange: PRIOR: prepend a compact faithful projection of the 2026-08-07 Infrastructure Promotion Rule: inherit mature mechanisms; if repeated mechanical burden remains add smallest owner-local projection; only repeated unowned stable semantic responsibility earns shared boundary; independent repo/service is a separate later gate.
independentOracle: Canonical later A0 and ACS closeouts, not the research prior itself.
developmentSplit: A0 Observation, A0 Configuration Identity, A0 Usage/Cost, ACS Runtime.
holdoutSplit: ACS Host, ACS Finance, ACS Security, ACS Workstation.
invalidityConditions: later disposition text leaks into packet
prior edited after first live call
invalid structured output scored as semantic error
new cases or replicas are added after observing results
authorityBoundary: Computing research only; no owner source mutation.
budget: DeepSeek V4 Flash and V4 Pro, two replicas per case/treatment/model: 8 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 64 logical trials; identical output/Harness budgets across treatments.
stopRule: Stop after 64 logical slots terminate. Analyze exact valid decisions, false-promotion severity, missed earned-local/shared changes and Provider token overhead. Do not tune the prior from the results.
deletionOrNoChangeOutcome: If the prior does not improve cumulative decision quality or mainly restates choices already obvious to strong models, do not treat meta-selection as a distinct PAL compounding mechanism.
publicationBoundary: A positive F5 may create a prospective meta-selection hypothesis in Computing; it does not authorize a global scheduler, architecture governor or owner policy.
